abaxx-technology-ag.name: abaXX Technology AG

rounds.round: early-stage financing (unnamed; company founded April 1999 with 3i and Earlybird money)
second financing round (General Atlantic Partners joins 3i and Earlybird)
third financing round (after the cancelled Neuer Markt IPO)

abaxx-technology-ag.status_detail: Acquired by Cordys (Putten, Netherlands) at the beginning of November 2007; price not disclosed. Cordys sold the abaXX e-banking unit to Crealogix in 2011.

valuation.basis: No priced figure of USD 1B or more. The cancelled November 2000 IPO would have given a market cap of 'fast 700 Millionen Mark' at the top of the range (Computerwoche 2000-12-15); the 2007 sale price was not disclosed.

abaxx-technology-ag.notes: Stuttgart maker of Java portal and process software for banks and public bodies. Earlybird is in from the start: the firm's April 1999 release already lists abaXX Technology GmbH, and Computerwoche says the company was 'mit Wagniskapital von der 3i Group sowie von Earlybird Venture Capital aus der Taufe gehoben' in 1999. No source names that round Seed, first round or Series A (the firm's 2007 release says only 'provided the early stage financing in 2000 with 3i as co-investor', and dates it 2000 against its own 1999 'Invested' year), so entry is null.

dooyoo-de-ag.name: dooyoo.de AG

entry.quote: übernahm im Dezember 1999 die erste institutionelle Finanzierungsrunde zusammen mit 3i Deutschland
entry.entry_asserted: The firm's own exit release dates its first money to the first institutional round of December 1999 and calls Earlybird the company's first investor ('seinem ersten Investor').

dooyoo-de-ag.status_detail: LeGuide.com S.A. (Paris) agreed to buy dooyoo in June 2008 and completed the purchase of 100% of the capital on 17 June 2008; price not disclosed.

valuation.basis: Sale price not disclosed; the company had 24 staff at the sale. No figure of USD 1B or more exists.

dooyoo-de-ag.notes: Berlin consumer-review and shopping-guide site (Germany, UK, Spain, Italy). The record calls Earlybird's entry the 'first institutional financing round' (December 1999, with 3i); no source calls it Seed or Series A. The live page gives Munich as HQ; the firm's own release and the archive say Berlin.

element-5-ag.name: element 5 AG

entry.quote: legten 3i und Earlybird mit einer Frühphasenfinanzierung im Rahmen der ersten institutionellen Finanzierungsrunde im Dezember 1999
entry.entry_asserted: The joint exit release of 3i, Earlybird and IKB says the two funded the first institutional round in December 1999 and calls it Earlybird's 'ursprüngliches Investment'.

rounds.round: second financing round (IKB Private Equity joins)

element-5-ag.status_detail: Digital River, Inc. bought element 5 on 19 April 2004 for USD 120M in cash, plus up to USD 2.5M earn-out.

valuation.basis: Signed acquisition price: Digital River's 8-K, 'for $120 million in cash'.

element-5-ag.notes: Cologne provider of outsourced e-commerce (online software sales) for software publishers, founded 1996. Unrelated to the Insight Partners row 'Element5' (San Jose, post-acute care, 2021); that sibling line is a name collision. Entry is the 'first institutional financing round' of December 1999 with 3i; no source calls it Seed or Series A.

interhyp.name: Interhyp

entry.amount: EUR 4.1M (Earlybird's amount in the first institutional round)
entry.quote: Interhyp, founded together with Earlybird as seed-investor in 1999
entry.entry_asserted: The firm calls itself the seed investor at the 1999 founding and says it 'invested in the first institutional financing round in September 1999'; the German release of 12.10.2005 gives EUR 4.1M for that round.

rounds.amount_native: Earlybird EUR 2.8M; round total not stated

graduation.later_round: second financing round (unnamed; 3i joined as a new institutional investor)
graduation.amount: Earlybird's part EUR 2.8M; total not stated
graduation.quote: In einer zweiten Finanzierungsrunde im Juli 2000, an der sich Earlybird mit 2,8 Mio. Euro beteiligte, kam 3i als weiterer institutioneller Investor hinzu.

interhyp.status_detail: IPO on 29 September 2005 (Frankfurt Prime Standard), then bought by ING Direct N.V. in 2008: public offer of EUR 64 a share announced 19 May 2008, 89.55% tendered by 24 July 2008. Now a subsidiary of ING Groep.

valuation.basis: Signed acquisition price: ING's offer of EUR 64 a share, 'für mehr als 400 Mio. Euro' (Der Standard); other press (MarketWatch, Bloomberg, Reuters headlines) give EUR 416M, about USD 647M. The firm's own 2007 release put the market cap at EUR 600M. Never USD 1B.

interhyp.notes: Munich online mortgage broker, founded June 1999 with Earlybird as seed investor; first-fund investment that returned more than 50x. The later round is unnamed and only Earlybird's EUR 2.8M share is stated, so the graduation rests on an unnamed round with a partial amount. The tender-result page is https://www.webwire.com/ViewPressRel.asp?aId=71250.

tipp24-ag.name: Tipp24 AG

rounds.round: early-stage financing (unnamed; the firm calls the next one the second round)
second financing round (led by Earlybird, with private investors)

tipp24-ag.status_detail: Listed since 12 October 2005; Tipp24 AG became Tipp24 SE (2009) and was renamed ZEAL Network SE (2014). Frankfurt/Xetra, ticker TIMA, ISIN DE000ZEAL241. Earlybird sold its last shares at the end of October 2007.

valuation.basis: Market cap today: 'a market cap or net worth of €850.33 million as of October 6, 2026' (stockanalysis.com); companiesmarketcap.com shows USD 0.94B for October 2026 (https://companiesmarketcap.com/zeal-network/marketcap/). The same stockanalysis page shows EUR 1.11B at 2025-12-30 and EUR 1.08B at 2024-12-30, which is above USD 1B at those dates; the judge decides whether a past year-end above USD 1B counts.

tipp24-ag.notes: Hamburg online lottery broker (today ZEAL Network SE: Lotto24, Tipp24). Earlybird's first money was EUR 3.7M in September 1999, which the firm calls only 'Early-Stage Finanzierung' / 'early stage financing'; the September 2000 round is 'the second round of financing'. No source names the 1999 round Seed, first round or Series A, so entry is null (it is the first round by implication only). Market cap is below USD 1B today but was about EUR 1.1B at the end of 2024 and 2025.

bridgeco.name: BridgeCo

entry.quote: As the seed financier, Earlybird is proud of BridgeCo’s track record of delivering new technology on time.
entry.entry_asserted: The January 2003 release on the second round quotes Earlybird partner Sabine Bendiek calling Earlybird 'the seed financier'; the firm's page gives 2000 as the investment and founding year.

rounds.lead: Benchmark Capital (new investor), with Earlybird, Infineon Ventures, Intel Capital

graduation.quote: BridgeCo AG is pleased to announce the successful conclusion of its second financing round of US$13.3 million, which closed in December 2002.

bridgeco.status_detail: SMSC (Standard Microsystems Corp.) acquired BridgeCo Inc. on 19 May 2011 for USD 40M in cash plus up to USD 27.5M in earn-outs.

valuation.native: USD 40M cash plus up to USD 27.5M
valuation.basis: Signed acquisition price in SMSC's 8-K press release.

bridgeco.notes: Networked-audio chips and software (founded 2000 in Zurich/Dübendorf, later headquartered in El Segundo, California). Earlybird was the seed financier in 2000; the next round is called only the 'second financing round' (USD 13.3M, December 2002, Benchmark Europe joining), so the graduation rests on an unnamed round with its amount. The live page's 'Chandler' is the acquirer's successor (Microchip), not BridgeCo.

smava.name: smava

entry.quote: Earlybird gibt heute den erfolgreichen Abschluss einer Finanzierungsrunde in Höhe von rund 4 Mio. EUR an smava
entry.entry_asserted: The firm's release of 14.05.2007 calls it Earlybird's second investment from the new fund Earlybird IV and smava's first established investors; deutsche-startups.de (2008-10-07) calls it 'der ersten Runde' ('In der ersten Runde sammelte smava ebenfalls rund vier Millionen Euro ein'). No source names it Seed or Series A.

rounds.lead: Earlybird, with business angels Gadowski, Glänzer, Jung, Schüpbach, Schwenke
Earlybird and Neuhaus Partners (existing) with Banca Sella (new)
Runa Capital, Verdane Capital, mojo.capital, with existing investors incl. Earlybird

smava.status_detail: smava GmbH, Berlin, operating; took over competitor Finanzcheck in 2021. A 2019 IPO plan was dropped.

valuation.basis: No priced figure of USD 1B or more. TechCrunch on the USD 65M round: 'According to sources, it is around $300 million with this round.'

smava.notes: Berlin consumer-loan marketplace, started 2007 as Germany's first peer-to-peer lending site. Earlybird IV led the first round (about EUR 4M, May 2007); the record never names it Seed or Series A, so the stage label 'Pre-Seed' on the live page has no support. Earlybird followed on in 2008, 2011 (holding 54% afterwards, per deutsche-startups.de) and 2016; the 2018 article does not name it.

clean-mobile-ag.name: Clean Mobile AG

entry.lead: Earlybird and SVTG (Silicon Valley Technology Group)
entry.quote: Earlybird announces the completion of a Series A financing round of € 3,3 million in Clean Mobile AG
entry.entry_asserted: The release says the round was led by Earlybird and SVTG, names HTGF as the existing seed investor, and counts Clean Mobile as the fifth company financed by the new Earlybird 2007 fund.

clean-mobile-ag.status_detail: Insolvent in early 2012 (Local Court of Munich, order of 02.02.2012, file 1504 IN 399/12); TQ-Systems GmbH (Seefeld) took over all assets and most staff in an asset deal in April 2012. The AG shell was liquidated; proceedings closed 27.04.2017.

valuation.basis: Insolvency and asset sale; no priced figure.

clean-mobile-ag.notes: Electric and hybrid drive systems for light vehicles (e-bikes, scooters), Unterhaching near Munich. Earlybird IV entered at the Series A; the seed was HTGF's. Insolvency followed by an asset sale to TQ-Systems, so 'acquired' with TQ as successor. Register record: https://www.northdata.com/Clean%20Mobile%20AG,%20Unterhaching/Amtsgericht%20M%C3%BCnchen%20HRB%20168585 (shareholder Earlybird GmbH & Co. Beteiligungs-KG IV).

kiwilogic-com-ag.name: Kiwilogic.com AG

rounds.round: first investment (unnamed; Earlybird is the 'existing partner' at the second round)
second round (reported in Work Study, April 2001; closing date not stated)
strategic stake by dtms AG (size not disclosed)
rounds.lead: dtms Deutsche Telefon- und Marketing Services AG

kiwilogic-com-ag.status_detail: Trade sale to Artificial Solutions Germany GmbH in August 2006 (the firm's exit list). The remaining Kiwilogic.com AG shell has been in liquidation since 14.08.2008.

valuation.basis: Price not disclosed; no figure of USD 1B or more.

kiwilogic-com-ag.notes: Hamburg maker of 'Lingubot' natural-language chatbots for websites; bought by Artificial Solutions (today Teneo.ai). Earlybird invested in 1999 and put in again in the EUR 5.2M second round with 3i (reported in Work Study, April 2001: 'completed its second round funding of 5.2 million Euros'); no source names the 1999 round, so entry is null. The live page's description (NFON, cloud telephony) and its 'Stockholm & Hamburg' HQ are wrong for this company; Stockholm is the acquirer's seat. Register: https://www.northdata.com/Kiwilogic%C2%B7com%20AG,%20Hamburg/HRB%2073714.

urbia-com.name: urbia.com

rounds.round: expansion capital (unnamed; Kennet Capital joins, Earlybird adds to its stake)

urbia-com.status_detail: urbia.com AG filed for insolvency in November 2001; Konzept Dialog GmbH (Neuwied) took the company over at the start of February 2002 and the filing was withdrawn. Later owned by Gruner + Jahr (the AG became G+J Parenting Media GmbH, merged into G+J Medien GmbH in 2019).

valuation.basis: Rescue takeover out of insolvency; no priced figure.

urbia-com.notes: Cologne family and parenting portal (content, forums), founded 1998, online since June 1999. Earlybird was in before February 2000: its release of 25.02.2000 says 'Kennet Capital steigt bei dem Wachstumsunternehmen ein, der deutsche Venture Capitalist Earlybird erweitert seine Beteiligung'. No source names or sizes Earlybird's first round, so entry is null. Searched: firm press archive, Computerwoche archive (5 items, none on financing), Bing/Google News '"urbia" Konzept Dialog', '"urbia" Earlybird', '"urbia.com" Earlybird', one web search. Second status source: https://www.onetoone.de/artikel/db/oto_35065.html ('hatte im November 2001 Insolvenz angemeldet, der Antrag konnte nun zurückgezogen werden'). Register: https://www.northdata.com/G+J%20Parenting%20Media%20GmbH,%20Hamburg/HRB%20131761.

conjectag.name: Conject

rounds.lead: Seventure Partners, with existing investor Earlybird

conjectag.status_detail: Aconex Limited (ASX: ACX, Melbourne) agreed to buy Conject on 17 March 2016 for EUR 65M in cash. The AG became Aconex AG and was merged into Oracle Deutschland in 2019.

valuation.basis: Signed acquisition price: 'Für die Übernahme legt Aconex 65 Millionen Euro auf den Tisch – in bar.'

conjectag.notes: Munich collaboration software for construction and real-estate projects. The firm's release of 7 March 2001 names Conject among the first 14 investments of Earlybird III, and the register lists Earlybird GmbH & Co. KG Parallel-Beteiligungskommanditgesellschaft III as shareholder (https://www.northdata.com/Aconex%20AG,%20M%C3%BCnchen/HRB%20130400). No source names or sizes the 2000 round, so entry is null. Total venture and growth capital 'over Euro 20 million' by 2008. Searched: firm press archive, Computerwoche archive, Bing/Google News '"conject" Earlybird Finanzierungsrunde', one web search.

oneshield.name: OneShield

rounds.lead: Bain Capital Credit and Pacific Lake Partners

oneshield.status_detail: OneShield Software operates independently from Marlborough, Massachusetts (site copyright 2026, no parent named). The 2020 and 2022 deals are described as growth investments, not a sale of the company. Earlybird's page shows 'Exit' from 2025, which is the firm leaving, not the company being acquired.

valuation.basis: No priced figure published for any round.

oneshield.notes: Core policy, billing and claims software for property and casualty insurers, founded 1999. Earlybird lists a 1999 investment and held it until 2025; I found no source that names or sizes the 1999 round, so entry is null. Searched: firm press archive (two 2008 customer releases only), Bing News '"OneShield" Earlybird' and '"OneShield" funding Earlybird', EDGAR full text '"OneShield" "Earlybird"' (0 hits), two web searches.

alloo-ag.name: Alloo AG

rounds.round: investment (unnamed, undated; capital increases were registered on 8 Jun 2000, 8 Dec 2000 and 7 Feb 2001)

alloo-ag.status_detail: The firm's exit list records a trade sale to Interwetten AG in July 2001 ('Verkauf an Interwetten AG'). The legal entity, alloo Interwetten AG (formerly WinTel Interwetten AG), went into liquidation on 20 November 2001 and was struck off on 27 June 2003.
alloo-ag.membership_detail: Not a sale-consideration row: Earlybird financed Alloo itself. Alloo was the Salzburg company alloo Interwetten AG (registered December 1998 as WinTel Interwetten GmbH, renamed alloo Interwetten AG in December 1999), which ran the betting and infotainment site alloo.com; the firm sold it to Interwetten AG in July 2001. I found no sign that Earlybird received Interwetten shares or put money into Interwetten afterwards; Interwetten never appears in the firm's portfolio lists.
alloo-ag.notes: Salzburg 'Internet infotainment channel' (bets on celebrities and events, alloo.com). Only the firm's own archived portfolio and exit lists tie Earlybird to it; no press on the investment was found, so entry round and year are unknown (the row's first_seen 2008 is a capture year). Register: https://www.northdata.com/alloo%20Interwetten%20AG,%20Salzburg/177919x. A pressetext article on alloo.com (https://www.pressetext.com/news/salzburger-wettplattform-macht-gottschalk-konkurrenz.html) returned 403 and was not read. Searched: Bing/Google News '"Alloo" Interwetten', '"alloo.com"', two web searches.

gmd.name: GMD

entry.quote: In 1999, Earlybird provided a first round of Venture financing to GMD Gesellschaft für Medizinische Datenbearbeitung.
entry.entry_asserted: The firm's December 2002 release dates it: 'In January 1999, Earlybird invested as Lead Investor in the early stage company GMD', followed by a second round in March 2000 and a third in February 2001 (https://index.commoncrawl.org/CC-MAIN-2008-2009-index?url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.earlybird.com%2Fde%2Fpress%2Frelease%2F213%2F&output=json).

gmd.status_detail: Dianoema S.p.A. (Bologna, later NoemaLife) acquired GMD, announced 11 December 2002. The GmbH was renamed NoemaLife GmbH in 2008 and is today Dedalus Labor GmbH, Bonn.

valuation.basis: No price published; Dianoema expected group revenue of EUR 10M for 2002.

gmd.membership_detail: Not a sale-consideration row: Earlybird financed GMD itself, as lead investor of the first round in January 1999. The sale-consideration position is the acquirer: Earlybird counts NoemaLife's May 2006 Milan IPO among its exits because GMD 'merged with NoemaLife's predecessor' in 2002, so its NoemaLife (Dianoema) shares came from selling GMD. I found no record of new Earlybird money into Dianoema or NoemaLife after the merger (firm releases of 2002 and 2006; Bing/Google News '"NoemaLife" Earlybird', '"Dianoema" GMD Earlybird').
gmd.notes: GMD Gesellschaft für medizinische Datenverarbeitung mbH: clinical workflow and electronic patient record software ('e-health.solutions'). Based in Cologne at Earlybird's entry (firm release of April 1999), registered in Munich from 2001 and at the sale, Berlin from 2004. The firm calls the entry the 'first round'; no source calls it Seed or Series A. Register: https://www.northdata.com/Dedalus%20Labor%20GmbH,%20Bonn/HRB%2026437.

identify-software-ltd.name: Identify Software Ltd.

rounds.amount_native: USD 15M at a USD 115M post-money valuation

rounds.round: investment by Earlybird III in 'Mutek Solutions' (unnamed)

identify-software-ltd.status_detail: BMC Software agreed on 27 March 2006 to acquire 100% of Identify Software Ltd for about USD 150M in cash.

valuation.basis: Signed acquisition price: 'BMC will pay approximately $150 million in cash for the shares.'

identify-software-ltd.notes: Israeli maker of AppSight, 'black box' software that records and diagnoses application failures; founded 1996 as MuTek Solutions Ltd. The firm's release of 7 March 2001 names 'Mutek Solutions' among the first 14 investments of Earlybird III and its page gives 2001 as the investment year. Ampal's 10-K405 for 2000 records a USD 15M round in October 2000 (USD 115M post-money) and an Intel 64 Fund investment in February 2001, but no source ties Earlybird to either by name, so entry is null. The MuTek to Identify link rests on the shared product name AppSight (Ampal 10-K405 for 2001 and BMC's release). Searched: EDGAR full text, Bing/Google News '"MuTek Solutions" raises', '"Identify Software" Earlybird', one web search.

light-blue-optics-ltd.name: Light Blue Optics Ltd.

entry.quote: today announced closing a US$26 million Series ‘A’ funding round, led by Earlybird Venture Capital and Capital-E
entry.entry_asserted: The release names 3i and NESTA as the existing investors (3i led the USD 3.5M seed) and Earlybird and Capital-E as the new leads; the firm's August 2008 release lists Light Blue Optics among the first investments of Earlybird IV.

rounds.round: financing of the successor business Kaptivo (unnamed)
rounds.lead: Draper Esprit, Benhamou Global Ventures, Generation Ventures

light-blue-optics-ltd.status_detail: Promethean bought Light Blue Optics' touch and gesture technology in September 2015 (the exit the firm records as 'Acquired by Promethean'). The remaining company traded as Kaptivo from 2016 and was acquired by Lifesize in August 2020. Light Blue Optics Limited (company 05018807) has been in members' voluntary liquidation since 6 January 2023.

valuation.basis: Neither sale price was published; the company 'had raised $50 million in financing since its launch in 2004' (TechCrunch, 2018).

light-blue-optics-ltd.notes: Cambridge (UK) developer of holographic laser projection, later interactive touch displays and the Kaptivo whiteboard camera. Earlybird IV co-led the Series A; the seed was 3i's. Sources read: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Promethean_World ('In September 2015, Promethean acquired touch and gesture technology from Light Blue Optics'), TechCrunch 2018 ('began life as a company called Light Blue Optics'), Companies House insolvency page https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/05018807/insolvency. The judge may prefer Promethean 2015 as the acquirer of record, since that is the firm's own exit.

graviton-inc.name: Graviton, Inc.

rounds.round: investment by Earlybird III (unnamed; held by 7 March 2001)

graviton-inc.status_detail: Graviton was dismantled and on 13 March 2003 sold its remote-monitoring assets to Xsilogy, Inc. (San Diego) for 3,036,317 Xsilogy common shares, 10% of Xsilogy, booked at USD 750,000, plus a conditional warrant. The firm records it as 'Merger with Xsilogy, Inc.' (May 2003). Xsilogy's assets were bought by SYS on 16 December 2004.

valuation.basis: Asset sale for stock booked at USD 750,000 (Xsilogy's audited statements); CNET in 2004 quotes the founder: 'the company fetched a measly $1 million'. The company had raised about USD 55M to 60M.

graviton-inc.membership_detail: Not a sale-consideration row: Earlybird financed Graviton itself. The firm's release of 7 March 2001 names Graviton among the first investments of Earlybird III, and the Series D release of August 2001 says 'Graviton's primary financial investors include venture capital firms Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers and Earlybird'. The Xsilogy shares were paid to Graviton, Inc. for its assets; Xsilogy would be the sale-consideration position. Xsilogy's audited 2003 and 2004 statements show no new equity round after the deal (only notes payable, later converted, and related-party notes), so nothing shows Earlybird putting new money into Xsilogy.
graviton-inc.notes: La Jolla (San Diego) developer of wireless sensor networks, 1999 to 2003. Earlybird III was in before the USD 35M Series D of August 2001 (CNET: 'a fourth round of funding, led by Merrill Lynch', total 'around $55 million'), but no source says which earlier round it joined, so entry is null. Press read: https://www.cnet.com/news/graviton-receives-35-million/ and https://www.cnet.com/news/building-a-wireless-nervous-system/ ('Its assets were sold last year to a company called Xsilogy'). SYS purchase: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/96057/000125994305000027/finalsb2.htm.

biovalve.name: Biovalve

rounds.round: Earlybird's investment was in Redeon, Inc. (unnamed, undated; before the 2001 merger)

biovalve.status_detail: BioValve Technologies, Inc. (Worcester, Massachusetts) put its drug-delivery device assets into Valeritas, LLC in August 2006 and was still a separate private company in 2008 (amended formation agreement). I found no record of a sale or dissolution; its Massachusetts registration is inactive and the Delaware entity is still listed. Earlybird's archived lists carry it until 2010.

valuation.basis: No priced figure of USD 1B or more.

biovalve.membership_detail: Earlybird backed Redeon, Inc. (Cambridge, Massachusetts; microneedle drug delivery), not BioValve. Redeon was taken over by BioValve Technologies in 2001: the firm's own release of 5 February 2002 lists its portfolio company as 'Redeon (merged with Biovalve)', and the CardioMEMS S-1/A says Redeon 'was subsequently acquired by Biovalve Technologies, Inc. in 2001' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1158091/000119312507057588/ds1a.htm). Earlybird therefore holds BioValve through the merger. I found no record of new Earlybird money into BioValve afterwards: the firm's press archive is silent, and the only EDGAR hits for 'BioValve' with 'Earlybird' are the SPAC underwriter EarlyBirdCapital's option in the 2006 Paramount Acquisition filings, which is a different firm.
biovalve.notes: BioValve Technologies: drug-delivery devices (h-Patch, Mini-Ject, microneedle patch), founded 1998; its device business became Valeritas. Status is the last known state, not a confirmed current one (registry listing read at https://opencorporates.com/companies?q=biovalve+technologies). Paramount's 2006 release on BioValve: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1330487/000104746906011334/a2172870zex-99_1.htm. Searched: firm press archive, EDGAR full text, Bing/Google News '"Redeon" BioValve merger', '"BioValve Technologies" Redeon', one web search.
